en: The Philippine archipelago contains exactly 7,641 islands, yet only about 2,000 of them are permanently inhabited by people.
Mayon Volcano in Albay is famous for having the most perfect cone shape of any active volcano in the world.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River features an underground river that flows directly into the sea, making it a navigable tidal river.
Lake Taal is the third largest lake in the Philippines and contains Volcano Island, which itself holds a smaller crater lake.
Mount Apo in Davao is the highest mountain in the Philippines, standing at 2,954 meters, and is home to the rare Philippine eagle.
The Cagayan River is the longest river in the Philippines, stretching 505 kilometers through the Cagayan Valley before emptying into the Babuyan Channel.
The Callao Cave in Cagayan contains a natural chapel illuminated by a hole in the ceiling, where sunlight shines directly onto the altar.
The Chocolate Hills in Bohol consist of at least 1,268 perfectly symmetrical cone-shaped hills that turn brown during the dry season.
The Philippine Trench reaches a maximum depth of 10,540 meters at the Galathea Depth, making it one of the deepest ocean trenches globally.
The Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park in the Sulu Sea is a UNESCO World Heritage site protecting over 600 species of fish and 360 species of coral.
The Philippines sits directly on the Pacific Typhoon Belt, causing the archipelago to experience an average of 20 tropical cyclones every single year.
The Banaue Rice Terraces in Ifugao were carved into the mountains by hand over 2,000 years ago and would stretch halfway around the globe if laid end-to-end.
